A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

power law shot noise exhibits the following properties: (1) the process is stationary, (2) the moments of the amplitude distribution are finite, (3) the amplitude probability density function is bounded, (4) the process has a power spectral density, and (5) the power spectral density is bounded.
the behavior of a power law shot noise process can be characterized in terms of the parameters of the process, the moments, and the autocorrelation functions of the process.
we have developed the theory for power law shot noise and have shown how the theory can be used to model the behavior of 1/f type shot noise.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the power law shot noise process, which has been used as a model for 1/f/super alpha noise, is not a good candidate as a model for such noise.
the behavior of power law noise is highly dependent on the choice of parameters, and that the power spectral density can be tailored to have 1/f type characteristics over a wide range of frequencies.

the moments, amplitude probability density function and autocorrelation function are all uniquely determined by the parameters of the process, so that the parameters can be estimated from the measured values of the moments, amplitude distribution, or autocorrelation function.
